text:
erica (oncall): FYI getting multiple customer escalation tickets, several 401s starting ~09:12 UTC. customers see "invalid_token" or "unknown key id". Investigating. :rotating_light:

jordan (cs): Customers: ACME (TKT-4821), NovaApps (TKT-4823). Both report sudden auth failures across many endpoints. They sent curl examples.

jordan (cs): curl example they sent:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_abc123" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{ "error": "invalid_token", "message": "unknown kid" }
```

deploy-bot: deploy finished: auth-service v2.3.1 -> prod at 09:08 UTC (build 0f3a7e).

devon (infra): Looking at auth-service metrics: spike in JWKS fetch errors starting 09:09, and token introspect 500s -> fallbacks -> 401s. Redis pubsub shows key-sync messages queued but large processing latency.

samir (engineer): Repro steps I ran in a dev cluster: rotate signing key, push new key to KMS, then call /introspect before the jwks endpoint republishes. If client hits introspect during window, we see kid mismatch and we return 401. I have a minimal repro: rotate then immediately validate -> 401.

linda (sre): Confirmed in logs: many new requests with error "kid not found" from introspect handler. Saw worker panics around jwks cache refresh; stacktrace points to cache invalidation race.

samir (engineer): Hypothesis: key rotation handler nukes local jwks cache then republishes asynchronously. If requests come in between, introspect tries to use fresh signer lookup but JWKS not available -> unknown kid. Looks like a regression introduced in v2.3.1 where we changed refresh flow.

erica (oncall): Impact: multiple enterprise customers seeing failed auth, some failing healthchecks. Severity P1. Opening incident.

incident-bot: Incident AUTH-312 created by erica (oncall) - AUTH service key sync regression. Incident channel: #inc-auth-312.

devon (infra): Quick mitigation options: 1) rollback auth-service to v2.3.0 (fast) 2) hotfix that reorders refresh to keep old cache until new jwks validated (safer) 3) increase cache TTL/grace so old keys accepted for extra window.

jordan (cs): Customers asking for ETA. Pushed note: "We're investigating; engineering has identified a key rotation regression and mitigation is in progress. Will update in 15m."

samir (engineer): I can prepare rollback PR now. Also prepping a hotfix branch that changes refresh to: fetch new JWKS -> validate keys -> atomically swap cache. That avoids nil window.

linda (sre): While we decide, we can temporarily enable a permissive fallback in the token validator to accept previous signing keys for +5m. That requires a config flip in config-store and rollout via ssm.

erica (oncall): Action plan: 1) devon to start rollback to v2.3.0 if rollback is quick. 2) samir to continue hotfix. 3) linda to apply permissive fallback toggle for immediate relief. 4) jordan to update customers.

devon (infra): Starting rollback now. I'll monitor error rate. Rolling back 2/3 pods to v2.3.0 first to avoid traffic flapping.

deploy-bot: rollback started: auth-service -> v2.3.0 rolling update at 09:28 UTC.

linda (sre): Applied permissive-fallback=true in config-store at 09:30 UTC; pushing config to auth-service. Expecting new config to be picked up by sidecar within ~30s.

samir (engineer): Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-service/pull/412 — changes JWKS refresh to atomic swap after validation. Adding unit + e2e tests.

devon (infra): Error rate dropping in the next 2min. 401s down ~70% already. JWKS fetch errors gone after rollback pods stabilized.

jordan (cs): Customers confirmed partial recovery: ACME reports API returning again, NovaApps still seeing intermittent 401s but much better. I'll mark tickets and escalate to enterprise success for postmortem.

erica (oncall): Good. Keep monitoring for 1h. Postmortem owners: samir (root cause + fix), devon (deploy/rollout), linda (oncall runbook update), jordan (customer comms).

samir (engineer): Root cause writeup notes: v2.3.1 introduced asynchronous jwks cache invalidation (change set 0f3a7e) which allowed a short window where the runtime had no jwks available. This surfaced as "unknown kid" in introspect path. Regression not caught by existing rotation e2e because test used warmed caches.

linda (sre): Immediate follow-ups: 1) add e2e that simulates rotation and immediate validate 2) add monitoring alert for jwks-fetch-errors > 5/m 3) ensure config toggle exists for fallback acceptance and documented TTL.

devon (infra): Long-term: implement atomic refresh + health-check gating on rollout so new build doesn't go live until jwks validated. Also add migration step to publish new key to jwks endpoint before switching active kid.

erica (oncall): I've updated incident tracker with short timeline and actions. Will keep channel open for updates and publish full postmortem after root cause confirmed.

jordan (cs): Customer follow-up messages queued. Suggest offering 2 weeks of credits for impacted enterprise customers.

samir (engineer): Merged hotfix to prod at 10:05 UTC after validation in canary. Monitor for regressions.

deploy-bot: deploy finished: auth-service v2.3.2 (hotfix) -> prod at 10:05 UTC (build 1a9c2d).

linda (sre): Error rate back to baseline by 10:12 UTC. No further 401 spikes. Marking incident as mitigated. Will start postmortem doc and link PRs/alerts.

erica (oncall): Incident mitigated. Closing active escalation but leaving postmortem open. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
